title: adj agent skill: adj ai skill --install

sections.heading: Why
sections.body: Agents need more than the 1800-byte AGENTS.md snippet from `adj ai` to use adj well: when to check before asking, how to word a question with options and a recommendation, which flags exist for narrowing reads (`--ref`, `--key-prefix`, `--max-bytes`, `--json`), and where the owner-only line sits (C27). Slicer already ships its skill with `slicer ai skill --install`; adj has no equivalent. Owner decisions (2026-11-02): one agent skill; delivered by the binary as `adj ai skill`; the `adj ai` snippet stays unchanged; extras are a name-check test, a reference file, a dogfood install and docs/release entries.

sections.heading: Files
sections.body:
- `internal/commands/ai.go` and `internal/commands/` (new embedded skill text beside `ai.md`, e.g. `skill.md`, plus a reference file for the skill folder).
- `internal/cli/ai.go` and `internal/cli/ai_test.go` (the `skill` subcommand; the existing no-flag, no-argument rule for `adj ai` stays).
- `.claude/skills/adj/`, `.agents/skills/adj/` and `.grok/skills/adj/` in this repo (dogfood install).
- `README.md`, `PROJECT.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`, `docs/json.md` if the command surface it pins changes.

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
- `adj ai skill` prints the SKILL.md and exits 0; it reads no repo and takes no `--root`; an unknown argument exits 2.
- `--output PATH` writes the text, creating parent directories; `--install` writes `.claude/skills/adj/`, `.agents/skills/adj/` and `.grok/skills/adj/` under the repo root (SKILL.md and the reference file); stdout lists the paths written; `--force` replaces a destination that holds different text, else a differing destination exits 1 and nothing is written; a second run with identical text changes nothing.
- Name-check test, like `ai_test.go` (C124, C125): fails if the skill or its reference names a command, flag or environment variable that does not exist.
- The skill states the owner-only commands (`decide`, `reject`, `supersede`, `inbox -i`, `renumber`, `init`, `import-adr`) and that an agent never runs them.
- `adj ai` output is byte for byte unchanged.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
Proposed, for the owner to overrule (C32 standing rule; record each as a catalog decision when settled):
- `adj ai skill [--output PATH] [--install] [--force]`, modelled on `slicer ai skill`. The skill text is embedded in the binary so it matches the installed version.
- One agent skill named `adj`: frontmatter `name` and `description` that trigger on deciding, asking the owner, or checking prior decisions; body covers check-before-ask and the four results, asking well (options, tradeoffs, recommendation, `--key`, `--ref`, `--recommend-text`), reading decisions (`context`, `show`, `list`, `--json`, `--max-bytes`), withdrawing or amending own open questions, the owner-only line, exit codes, and what to tell the owner (no repo, duplicate ID).
- A reference file in the skill folder with the command, exit-code and JSON-shape detail, so SKILL.md stays short.
- Install this repo's own copy with `adj ai skill --install`.
- README, PROJECT.md and CHANGELOG entries. `adj ai` and its 1800-byte snippet are not changed.

Settled by the owner (2026-11-02, adj 20 `ai.skill-flags`, adj 21 `ai.skill-install-scope`): the skill may name flags the snippet omits for size (e.g. `context --max-bytes`), and `--install` is project-only (use `--output PATH` for other destinations).

Owner decisions (2026-11-02): S54 is in pass 1.0 and S39 depends on it.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body: `go test ./...`; `go vet ./...`; `gofmt -l cmd internal` prints nothing; `adj lint`; `adj ai` output unchanged; `adj ai skill --install` into a temp root writes the three destinations.
